newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to emphasise foreign borrowing, cut yields.
newsitem.headline: Russia to emphasise foreign borrowing, cut yields.

text.p: The Russian government will shift the emphasis of its borrowing to foreign markets from domestic markets, and aims to bring yields on government securities down to 20-25 percent in the second half of this year, a senior central bank official said on Thursday.

"That is the minimum level at which interest from both Russian and foreign investors can be preserved," Konstantin Korishchenko, head of the bank's open-market operations department, told an investment conference.
Russian yields are currently about 30-32 percent.
Korishchenko noted that the volume of Finance Ministry borrowing was a prime determinant of domestic yields, but another major factor was bank liquidity.

"Today the government securities market is actually the sole means of regulating bank liquidity. And all the problems arising from liquidity have an effect on T-bill yields and to a lesser extent on the currency market," he said.
